title: A Journal of Discoveries
paragraphs: A reading group was assembling a journal of discoveries from its recent work. The discoveries were not all inventions or journeys to distant places. Sometimes they involved noticing a choice, recognizing a pattern, or understanding why a seemingly minor event deserved closer attention.

The group began by reading the following accounts without adding explanations of its own. A glint of sunlight reflected from the window. It is unkind to gloat when an opponent makes a mistake. The fable portrayed gluttony as a failure of self-control. The old tree had a thick, gnarled trunk.

It then considered a second group of accounts, looking for both similarities and differences. The rival's taunts could goad him into a rash decision. A sharp stone can gouge the soft wood. The gourmet could identify the unusual herbs in the dish. The dancer made a graceful turn across the stage.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.
